items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: John Baldwin had come I think a few years before and of course was starting his reign as just an outstanding choir director... I don’t know if you ever were fortunate to hear John play the organ but he really was a wonderful musician.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well when you were here was there an active music department?

Very much so. John Baldwin had come I think a few years before and of course was starting his reign as just an outstanding choir director, a technically just stupendous organist. I don’t know if you ever were fortunate to hear John play the organ but he really was a wonderful musician. And so there was that, and then there was the jazz which I’m sure we’ll get into. And then Berrian Shute was the old professor of music and used to have us down to his home and we’d listen on the old scratchy 78 records in the…

Do you think there’s a difference now with — music is so available in huge quantities to younger people through iPods and internet and the whole thing, where during your era and my era it was not so getable all the time. Do you think it makes a difference?
